messages:
oliver: Quick update — reproduced odd kernel pick on SM80 where selector prefers flashv3 noncausal kernels for causal workloads with head_dim=30, then falls back to v2 slowpath; observed ~12% p99 regression on convo workload.

maria: ugh. do you have a repro script or traces?

oliver: paste below. simple request stream with seqlen=128, microbatch=2, kv_cache enabled. attached perf snapshot link: https://redwood.internal/perf/1729994444

sam: can you share the profiler output (nvprof/cupti) and kernel names?

oliver: profiler snippet:
```
Kernel: flashv3_causal_pad_remap head=30 seq=128 sm=80 time=1.82ms
Fallback: flashv2_slow_causal time=2.05ms
Observed: selector tried flashv3 (failed to allocate temp tile) -> fallback to v2
Note: KV cache warmup increases temp allocations by ~20% on first few steps
```

katie: sounds like allocator threshold triggers because of pad remap buffer growth from kv cache. maybe selector should probe with kv_cache flag earlier.

maria: Is this only at head_dim=30? we have heuristics around multiples of 8/16.

oliver: yes — head_dim % 8 != 0 seems to push flashv3 into a path that needs remap. head=32 uses fastpath and is fine. head=30 hits remap + temp tile + spills.

bench-bot: quick-bench results: (microbatch=2, seq=128)
- head=32: p99=28ms
- head=30: p99=31.4ms (+12%)
- head=30 no-kv: p99=29ms

sam: temporary mitigation — add a selector rule: if head_dim%8 != 0 and kv_cache enabled -> prefer flashv2 until remap memory path optimized. Can we flip that via config?

oliver: yes, we can set env: REDWOOD_KERN_SELECTOR_OVERRIDE=prefer_v2_for_unaligned_heads

katie: longer term: we should add a small runtime probe that measures remap temp usage per model and caches a boolean per model+seqlen+kv flag. If temp_alloc > threshold -> pick v2. avoids guessing by head_dim alone.

maria: agree. also add telemetry counter so we can alert when selector falls back more than X%.

deploy-bot: deploy started: kernel-selector-hotfix -> rolling to canary (5% of runtime nodes)

oliver: thanks. i'll open a tiny PR with probe + telemetry and include the repro and perf table.

sam: assign to runtime-kernel team, tag me. good catch.

katie: cc: @infra-scheduler to watch canary for memory OOMs.

oliver: adding notes to the incident board and link to PR: https://redwood.internal/pull/4821

maria: :thumbsup:
